title.narrative: NIHR DA 1: Towards Reducing Unnecessary C-Section via System Transformation in Bangladesh (TRUST).

description.narrative:
A low- and middle-income country (LMIC) award, led by the International Centre for Diarrheal Disease Research, Bangladesh (ICDDR,B) which aims to address the issue of unnecessary caesarean sections (C-sections) in Bangladesh.
In recent years, Bangladesh has seen an alarming rise in C-sections in contrast to normal vaginal delivery. While C-sections can be lifesaving in certain circumstances, unnecessary C-sections carry significant risks and costs, making it a priority for the government and stakeholders in Bangladesh to reduce these procedures where appropriate. Although some progress has been made in policies and guidelines, along with increasing midwives and improving public maternity services for normal delivery, many women still opt for private facilities where vaginal births are significantly less common.
Understanding of the factors driving high C-section rates in Bangladesh remains incomplete. While profit incentives play a role, the issue is more complex. Further work is needed to identify these drivers and potential actions. The ultimate goal of the project is to collaboratively design a research programme aimed at developing and testing novel solutions for reducing unnecessary C-sections.
Commencing in January 2025, the twelve-month award will involve the review and compilation of existing research, before holding workshops with key stakeholder groups, including urban and rural women, midwives, nurses, obstetricians, women's health organisations, and policymakers. The award team will facilitate dialogues with diverse stakeholders in order to develop a shared understanding of the current situation and potential strategies for improvement. Individuals interested in joining a multi-stakeholder research team to develop a detailed follow-on research plan will be identified. Additionally, the award focuses on strengthening the research capacity and confidence of Bangladeshi researchers to lead large-scale research programmes.

The award has five objectives:
1. Summarise existing research on recent C-section patterns and drivers in Bangladesh, and interventions to reduce unnecessary C-sections. 2. Integrate stakeholder perspectives with research evidence to develop a shared understanding of the scale, drivers, and possible actions for unnecessary C-sections. 3. Build a consortium of individuals equipped to design and implement a new applied research programme. 4. Design a follow-on research programme to develop, pilot, and evaluate novel approaches to reducing unnecessary C-sections. 5. Strengthen health research capacity in Bangladesh.
